title: Luke Bible Quiz - Chapter 13
description: Ten questions on Luke 13: the barren fig tree, the woman healed on the Sabbath, the mustard seed and the narrow door.

questions.text: What had Pilate done, according to those who spoke to Jesus?
questions.explanation: They told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

answers.text: He had made the tower in Siloam fall on eighteen men
He had mixed the Galileans' blood with their sacrifices
He had forbidden sacrifices in Jerusalem
He had sent Pharisees to warn him

questions.text: For how long had the owner come looking for fruit on the fig tree?
questions.explanation: He said, "These three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none."

answers.text: One year
Seven years
Eighteen years
Three years

questions.text: What did the vine dresser ask to be allowed to do with the fig tree?
questions.explanation: The vine dresser asked that the tree be left alone for one more year, while he dug around it and fertilized it.

answers.text: Leave it one more year so he could fertilize it
Cut it down and plant another in its place
Move it out of the vineyard into the garden
Water it every day for three years

questions.text: How long had the woman in the synagogue had a spirit of infirmity?
questions.explanation: The text says she had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, was bent over, and could in no way straighten herself up.

answers.text: Twelve years
Three years
Eighteen years
Since her birth

questions.text: Why was the ruler of the synagogue indignant?
questions.explanation: He was indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, and said that there are six days in which men ought to work.

answers.text: Because the woman had not asked permission
Because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath
Because Jesus taught in parables
Because the multitude rejoiced

questions.text: What did he compare God's Kingdom to, that a man put in his own garden?
questions.explanation: He said God's Kingdom is like a grain of mustard seed which a man put in his own garden, which grew and became a large tree where the birds of the sky live.

answers.text: A fig tree planted in a vineyard
A narrow door in a house
A grain of mustard seed
A vineyard with a vine dresser

questions.text: In how many measures of flour did the woman hide the yeast?
questions.explanation: He said the Kingdom is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened.

answers.text: Seven
Twelve
Two
Three

questions.text: What did he tell them to strive to enter in by?
questions.explanation: He told them to strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many will seek to enter in and will not be able.

answers.text: The narrow door
The gate of the vineyard
The door of the synagogue
The way to Jerusalem

questions.text: What did some Pharisees warn him about on that same day?
questions.explanation: Some Pharisees came and told him to get out and go away, because Herod wanted to kill him.

answers.text: That the crowd would stone him
That the tower in Siloam would fall
That Herod wanted to kill him
That Pilate had forbidden him to teach

questions.text: What did he compare himself to when he spoke about gathering Jerusalem's children?
questions.explanation: He said he had often wanted to gather her children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and they refused.

answers.text: A farmer sowing his seed
A hen gathering her brood under her wings
A shepherd leading his sheep to water
A vine dresser pruning a tree
